book_title: The Epistle of Paul to Philemon.

verses.text: <sc>PAVL</sc> the prisoner of Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>, and brother Timothee: to Philémon the beloued and our coadiutor,
& to Appia our deerest sister, & to Archippus our felow-souldiar and to the church vvhich is in thy house.
Grace to you and peace from God our father, and our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
I giue thankes to my God, alvvaies making a memorie of thee in my praiers,
hearing thy <na>[1]</na> charitie and faith vvhich thou hast in our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc>, and tovvard al the sainctes:

notes.text: Faith and charitie commended alwais together, both necessarie to make a complete Christian man, and to iustification & saluation.

verses.text: that the communication of thy faith may be made euident in the agnition of al <na>[1]</na> good that is in you in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>.
For I haue had great ioy and consolation in thy charitie, because the bovvels of the sainctes <na>[1]</na> haue rested by thee brother.

notes.text: The dueties of charitie and mercie done to Christes prisoners, are exceding acceptable to God and al good men.

verses.text: For the vvhich thing hauing great confidence in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc> to commaund thee that vvhich pertaineth to the purpose:
for charitie rather I beseeche, vvhereas thou art such an one, as Paul being old and now prisoner also of <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ.
I beseeche thee for my sonne vvhom I haue begotten in bandes, <cr>[1]</cr> Onesimus,
vvho hath been sometime vnprofitable to thee, but now profitable both to me & thee,
vvhom I haue sent backe to thee. And <na>[1]</na> do thou receiue him as mine ovvne bovvels.

notes.text: Al Spiritual men ought to be exceding propense and ready to procure mens pardon, and reconciliation to al penitents.

verses.text: whom I would haue reteined vvith me, that for thee he might minister to me in the bandes of the Gospel:
but vvithout thy counsel I vvould doe nothing: that thy good might be not as it vvere of necessitie, but voluntarie.
For perhaps therfore he departed for a season from thee, that thou mightest take him againe for euer.
novv not as a seruant, but for a seruant, a most deere brother, especially to me, but hovv much more to thee both in the flesh and in our Lord?
If therfore thou take me for thy fellow: receiue him as my self.
And if he hath hurt thee any thing or is in thy dette, that impute to me.
I Paul haue vvritten vvith mine ovvne hand: I vvil repay it: not to say to thee, <na>[1]</na> that thou ovvest me thine ovvne self also.

notes.text: The great debt & duetie that we owe to such as be our spiritual parents in Christ.

verses.text: Yea brother. <na>[1]</na> cGod graunt I may enioy thee in our Lord. Refresh my bovvels in our Lord.
Trusting in thy obedience I haue vvritten to thee, knovving that thou vvilt doe aboue that also vvhich I do say.
And withal prouide me also a lodging. for I hope by your praiers that I shal be giuen to you.
There salute thee Epaphras my fellow-prisoner in Christ <sc>IESVS</sc>,
Marke, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke my coadiutors.
The grace of our Lord <sc>IESVS</sc> Christ be with your spirit. Amen,

chapters.summary: Hearing of Philémons vertue, who was a Colossian, he writeth a familiar letter from Rome (being prisoner there) about his fugitiue seruant Onesimus: not doubting but that he might commaund him, yet rather requesting that he wil forgiue him, yea and receiue him as he would Paul him self, who also hopeth to come vnto him.
